content.comment_body: Hello, I'm currently working with [product_name] software for my [product_name] PLCs. I want to connect my PLC to my computer to monitor the plant, but I'm unsure about which solution to use, similar to [product_name]. I’m looking for a PLC that allows PC connection and program execution, without needing an HMI. I’m considering a [version_no] but I’m not certain if that’s the right choice.
I'm looking for a way to view plant data on my PC connected to a PLC, ideally without an HMI. Can this PLC be programmed with [product_name] software, or is another software required?

The current [product_name] version [version_no] integrates two web servers—a basic and an advanced version. The basic web server replicates the PLC display (or [product_name] operator panel) and provides a virtual keyboard. The advanced web server lets you build custom browser websites using the free [product_name] web development program.
Check out this [company_name] demonstration video featuring web server functionality through [product_name].

Hi, it's difficult to give detailed advice without more information. Your image resembles a SCADA system running on a PC. You should first clarify the SCADA software and the compatible controllers. [product_name] can handle S7-communication and ModbusTCP; if your SCADA supports these, it’s a viable option. If you aren't using SCADA and simply want an overview, follow the recommendations from [user_name]. In that case, you can use the [product_name] web server to build such web pages. Hope this helps.

You can use tools like LabVIEW, My Open Lab, or NI Measurement Studio with the Modbus TCP protocol alongside [product_name] or [version_no] PLCs, or any PLC supporting these communication protocols. Alternatively, with S7Comm protocol, the SNAP7 library can be partnered with NI Measurement Studio and Visual Studio in C# or VB.NET.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants want a simple way to connect a PLC to a PC for monitoring and programming tasks, seeking solutions that do not require an HMI or complex SCADA setup. There is uncertainty about matching hardware and software, protocol support, and how to best use built-in web servers for monitoring. Some users are unsure if their current software tools are sufficient for these tasks.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate an easy connection of the PLC to a PC for visual monitoring, with programming managed through familiar [company_name] software, without relying on extra equipment like HMIs or additional software.
